summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education: discrete mathematics (integers, modular arithmetic, gcd and primes, binomial coefficients, induction), algorithms (big-O and related asymptotic notation, divide-and-conquer recurrences, the RAM and multitape Turing models), elementary linear algebra over the reals and F_2 (vector spaces, linear maps, rank, dot products, matrix products), complex numbers with their modulus and polar form, and polynomials with their coefficient products. This goes as far as the introductory level in each, enough to read the algorithmic and combinatorial parts of the paper, but not into specialist algebra, tensor products, bilinear forms, or numerical analysis.

known.name: Logarithms
known.gloss: The logarithm log_b x is the exponent to which the base b must be raised to give x, and the base-2 logarithm counts the bits needed to write a number.

known.name: Big-Omega, big-Theta and little-o notation
known.gloss: Omega(f) bounds a function below by a constant multiple of f for large inputs, Theta(f) bounds it both above and below, and o(f) means the ratio to f tends to zero.

known.name: Floor and ceiling functions
known.gloss: The floor of x is the largest integer not exceeding x, and the ceiling of x is the smallest integer not below x.

known.name: Positional (radix) representation
known.gloss: A nonnegative integer written in base b is a finite string of digits, each between 0 and b-1, whose value is the sum of digit times the corresponding power of b.

known.name: Bitwise XOR
known.gloss: XOR of two bits is 1 exactly when the bits differ, and bitwise XOR of two equal-length bit strings applies this to each position.

known.name: Hamming weight
known.gloss: The Hamming weight of a bit string is the number of positions that hold a 1.

known.name: Modular arithmetic and congruences
known.gloss: Two integers are congruent modulo m when they differ by a multiple of m, and arithmetic on the residue classes modulo m is well defined by working with representatives.

known.name: Greatest common divisor and coprime integers
known.gloss: The gcd of two integers is the largest integer dividing both, and two integers are coprime when their gcd is 1.

known.name: Prime numbers
known.gloss: A prime is an integer greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and itself, and every integer greater than 1 factors uniquely into primes.

known.name: Binomial coefficients
known.gloss: The binomial coefficient binom(n,k) counts the k-element subsets of an n-element set, and equals n!/(k!(n-k)!).

known.name: Indicator vector of a set
known.gloss: The indicator vector of a subset S of a finite set has entry 1 at each element of S and 0 elsewhere.

known.name: Dot product and orthogonal vectors
known.gloss: The dot product of two vectors of the same length is the sum of the products of their corresponding entries, and two vectors are orthogonal when this sum is zero.

known.name: Matrix product, transpose, diagonal and triangular matrices
known.gloss: The product of an m-by-k and a k-by-n matrix is the m-by-n matrix of dot products of rows and columns, the transpose swaps rows and columns, and a diagonal or triangular matrix has zeros off its diagonal or on one side of it.

known.name: Field of two elements
known.gloss: The field F_2 has the two elements 0 and 1, with addition given by XOR and multiplication by AND.

known.name: Sequence convolution
known.gloss: The convolution of two finite sequences is the sequence whose k-th term is the sum of products of terms whose indices add to k, which is the coefficient list of the product of the corresponding polynomials.

known.name: Divide-and-conquer recurrence
known.gloss: A divide-and-conquer recurrence expresses the cost of an input of size n in terms of the costs of smaller subproblems plus the cost of combining them, and its solution is found by unrolling the recursion.

known.name: Geometric series
aliases: sum of powers of a ratio
known.gloss: A geometric series is a sum of the form a + ar + ar^2 + ... + ar^k, which equals a(1 - r^(k+1))/(1 - r) when r is not 1 and is bounded by a constant over 1 - r when |r| < 1.

known.name: Mathematical induction
known.gloss: Induction proves a statement for all natural numbers by proving it for a base case and showing that it holds for n+1 whenever it holds for n (or for all smaller values, in strong induction).

known.name: Random-access machine model
known.gloss: The random-access machine has a finite program and memory cells addressed by integers, so that any cell can be read or written in one step.

known.name: Fixed-point arithmetic
known.gloss: A fixed-point number is an integer scaled by a fixed power of two, so that arithmetic on such numbers is integer arithmetic with a fixed binary point.

known.name: Complex modulus and polar form
aliases: absolute value of a complex number
known.gloss: The modulus |a+bi| of a complex number is sqrt(a^2+b^2), its conjugate is a-bi, and every nonzero complex number can be written as r times e^(i theta) with r > 0 and a real angle theta.
